A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CreataSet/CrEval study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original human-annotation results, evaluator comparisons, training ablations, out-of-distribution evaluation, and creativity-enhancement experiments in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and adds benchmark evaluations, diagnostic analyses, and human assessments in Section 4 and Appendix A.

M1.justification: The data-construction pipeline, pseudo-labeling heuristics, classification objective, response swapping, negative sampling, and three-way inference remain unchanged. Bradley-Terry training and omission of response swapping appear as new experimental comparisons. Explicitly documenting both Qwen backbones and k=5 does not establish a method revision.

E1.justification: V2 adds WritingPrompts and the Alternative Uses Task to the retained creative-writing generalization evaluation (Section 4.4). Appendix A.4.5 additionally evaluates creativity-enhanced models on MATH, HumanEval, and TruthfulQA, extending coverage to mathematical reasoning, code generation, and truthfulness. CreataSet's original coverage remains unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds Creativity Index and replaces Gemini-2.0-Pro/Flash with Gemini-2.5-Pro/Flash. The retained creative-writing OOD comparison drops Qwen2.5-14B/72B, LLaMA3.1-70B, Gemma-3-12B/27B, and Prometheus-13B (v1 Figure 9; v2 Figure 8). Appendix A.4.2 adds a Bradley-Terry loss comparator. LitBench is discussed but is not evaluated as an evaluator baseline.

E3.justification: Section 3.3 replaces validation using 50 response pairs per model/prompt combination with a description specifying 150 groups and 1,050 pairs. New protocols select 213 WritingPrompts pairs using a like-count gap greater than 10 and 541 AUT pairs using a human-score gap greater than two. The appendices add defined pilot/diversity assessments and TruthfulQA metrics. These changes do not establish rerunning the retained main experiments.

E4.justification: V2 adds a response-swapping ablation, classification-versus-Bradley-Terry loss comparison, absolute-scoring pilot, response-diversity assessment, analysis of attributes associated with CrEval choices, and success/failure cases. It also tests whether creativity tuning compromises reasoning or truthfulness. The original data-composition, data-scale, backbone, and DPO difficulty analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain deterministic evaluation and ICC-based annotation-reliability reporting. Neither documents repeated training runs, random seeds, confidence intervals, or a significance-testing procedure. V2 calls the newly reported reasoning differences statistically nonsignificant, but provides no test details; this is an added significance outcome rather than a documented statistical-method change.

E6.justification: Pseudo-label validation accuracies change from 90.4%/87% to 86.6%/81.4% under the revised sampling description. V2 newly reports CrEval-7B F1/agreement of 58.22%/45.54% on WritingPrompts and 92.46%/78.37% on AUT, plus diagnostic and capability-preservation results. Gemini results are replaced for newer model versions, and the CrEval-14B OOD result is removed. Main Table 2 CrEval scores and existing DPO results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation 1, the pairwise formulation, and the two pseudo-labeling assumptions are retained. The new Bradley-Terry discussion is explanatory and empirical; it introduces no formal derivation, theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows the novelty claim from the first cross-domain pairwise creativity evaluator to being among the first. The principal claims about CreataSet, human alignment, domain generalization, and using CrEval to enhance creativity remain.

C2.justification: Appendices A.1–A.2 add substantive arguments about subjectivity, consensus versus conformity, and pairwise versus absolute assessment. Appendices A.4–A.5 add interpretations of creative attributes, subtle-preference failures, and preservation of reasoning and truthfulness. V2 explicitly identifies the dataset as predominantly Simplified Chinese and discusses linguistic applicability. The original limitations and societal-impact passages are retained.

D1.justification: V2 documents k=5, taxonomy construction, both Qwen backbones, and annotator recruitment, demographics, and compensation. Core hyperparameters, hardware, and prompt templates are retained, while the DPO evaluation's explicit three-rater count is omitted. The new Reproducibility Statement claims public code, data, and models, although Appendix A.3.2 retains future-release wording; actual availability is unresolved by the PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 adds discussion of Creativity Index, LitBench's specialized reward models, and critical work on creativity evaluation, alongside additional psychological literature supporting its consensus-based framing. These refine comparisons and qualify novelty while preserving the central positioning as a cross-domain, text-level LLM evaluator.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites paragraphs in the introduction, related work, method overview, and results discussion. The separate A–G appendices are reorganized into one Appendix A with eleven subsections. Ethics, reproducibility, and LLM-usage statements are added, alongside revised headings and conference-status text.

P2.justification: The OOD mirrored bar chart becomes three heatmaps, Table 2 gains improvement rows and colored highlighting, and five appendix tables are added. The consistency plot gains an ablation bar. V1 Figure 5 moves to the appendix as v2 Figure 11, with other plots resized or repositioned. The conference template also changes title treatment, headers, typography, and layout.

improvement.justification: V2 materially strengthens v1's narrow external validation, previously limited to 36 creative-writing pairs, and addresses its lack of checks on other capabilities after creativity tuning. The added AUT/WritingPrompts evaluations, loss and position ablations, reasoning/TruthfulQA checks, and failure examples provide substantial supporting and diagnostic evidence. These gains outweigh the removal of larger-model OOD comparisons, although popularity-based labels and underspecified statistical claims limit the strength of some conclusions.
